children: Over the first five months of this fiscal year, Japanese investors bought almost as many coupon-bearing domestic government bonds as they did in all of fiscal year 2025, while foreign purchases have nearly dried up, according to Japan Securities Dealers Association data.

Domestic investors bought 21.7 trillion yen ($137.17 billion) of coupon Japanese government bonds (JGBs) from April through August, 89% of fiscal 2025's 24.3 trillion yen total, JSDA's latest data on Thursday indicated.
Japan's fiscal year runs from April 1 through March 31.
Their purchases are on pace to exceed the 33.9 trillion yen level seen in fiscal year 2024, the highest in the data set going back to fiscal 2018, when JSDA revised its reporting format.
Medium-term JGBs were the primary target, with domestic investors snapping up 12.7 trillion yen of the securities from April through August, compared with 9.1 trillion yen in all of fiscal 2025.
Domestic investors bought 3.6 trillion yen of super-long-term JGBs, roughly matching fiscal 2025's full-year total and far below the peak of 19 trillion yen seen in fiscal 2021.
Foreign investors bought 2.8 trillion yen of coupon JGBs from April through August, compared with 32.8 trillion yen in fiscal 2025, their largest annual total in the data set.
Foreigners were net sellers of medium-term JGBs, offloading 1.9 trillion yen of the securities after net purchases of 17.4 trillion yen in fiscal 2025.
